note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Controlled corruption of stories enables evaluating feedback quality

nodes.name: Feedback task is under-studied
nodes.description: Providing open-ended writing feedback (praise, criticism, suggestions) is an under-studied LLM task that differs from text continuation or rewriting because the model generates no content itself and guides the writer to fix the writing.

nodes.name: Few resources for non-academic feedback
nodes.description: Existing resources for studying LLM feedback focus on academic domains such as peer review and essay writing, so little exists for creative story writing.

nodes.name: Controlled corruption of stories
nodes.description: About 1,300 stories (326 each of original, backtranslated, swapped-sentence and deleted-sentence versions) are built by corrupting 326 short seed stories from ROCStories and BIG-bench datasets, with backtranslation applied ten times.

nodes.name: STORYFEEDBACK dataset
nodes.description: The STORYFEEDBACK dataset contains about 84k pairs of stories and feedback generated by eight LLMs under four prompt types in zero-shot and two-shot settings.

nodes.name: Four evaluation questions
nodes.description: Feedback is evaluated on whether it is well-formed and specific, correct (suggestions improve the story), identifies the biggest problem, and gives positive comments appropriately.

nodes.name: Human annotation protocol
nodes.description: 1,920 pieces of feedback, evenly distributed over models, corruptions and prompt types, were rated by three annotators each on dimensions such as correctness, error-detection, relevance and perfect-agree.

nodes.name: Models give valid specific feedback
nodes.description: Models score highly on sanity-check, specificity and correctness questions in human evaluation, so their feedback is generally well-formed, story-specific and mostly helpful.

nodes.name: Models miss the biggest issue
nodes.description: Error-detection and relevance scores are much lower than correctness: models often miss the most salient problem and do not address the intentionally introduced corruptions, commenting on smaller issues instead.

nodes.name: Models say perfect-as-is wrongly
nodes.description: Models are not discerning with positive comments: when they call a story perfect-as-is, annotators frequently disagree (low perfect-agree), and the Table 1 automatic precision of 'perfect as-is' is below 1.

nodes.name: Larger models more precise
nodes.description: Larger model versions are more precise in using the 'perfect as-is' option than smaller counterparts, and Gemma and Gemini are most precise but rarely use the option.

nodes.name: Humans differ from models in feedback type
nodes.description: Annotators are more likely than models to say there are no issues (especially for original stories) and give different categories of feedback, per Fig 5.

nodes.name: Future work: salient issues
nodes.description: Future work should identify the most salient writing issues rather than merely providing correct feedback, and extend evaluation to long-form writing.

isolated_nodes.name: Corruption methods differ in difficulty
isolated_nodes.description: Backtranslated stories receive higher correctness, error-detection and relevance scores than other corruption types, while relevance is where models struggle most when corrupted stories contain swaps or deletions (Table 4).

isolated_nodes.name: Bulleted-list prompts help
isolated_nodes.description: Prompting for a bulleted list (BL only and BL full) yields different, generally better-rated outputs than other prompts (Table 5).

isolated_nodes.name: Spot-the-problem prompt worst
isolated_nodes.description: Prompting the model to 'spot the problem' yields the lowest correctness and error-detection scores (Table 5).

isolated_nodes.name: Few-shot no clear gain
isolated_nodes.description: Two-shot prompting shows no clear improvement over zero-shot in human scores, and two-shot models often repeat the feedback in the examples.

isolated_nodes.name: Two-shot more precise on PAI
isolated_nodes.description: Two-shot feedback is more precise in using 'perfect as-is' than zero-shot, possibly because one few-shot example is labeled that way.

isolated_nodes.name: Larger models more diverse
isolated_nodes.description: Larger model versions produce more diverse feedback (lower trigram repetition) than smaller ones, with Gemma and Gemini most diverse.

isolated_nodes.name: Annotator agreement moderate to high
isolated_nodes.description: Krippendorff's alpha is moderate to high for most dimensions, lowest for perfect-agree because judging a text as already good is subjective.

isolated_nodes.name: Closed models outperform open
isolated_nodes.description: Closed-source models outperform open-source models (particularly Bloom) on most human metrics, with the best closed models performing similarly.

isolated_nodes.name: Study scope limited
isolated_nodes.description: The study covers only English short stories with synthetic writing issues, eight LLMs and four prompts, and single-turn feedback.

structural_reasoning: Motivation and data construction lead to the human-evaluation findings, which motivate the future-work recommendation; prompt, model and annotation side-analyses are isolated.
